top_categories.workout_context: 91ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
7,464ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo La Nucia's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.

Road-specific control matters at Granfondo La Nucia. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 82 miles.
At Granfondo La Nucia, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo La Nucia. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 82, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
7,464ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 82 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo La Nucia. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 82 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.weather: October in La Nucia, Alicante, Spain. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Granfondo La Nucia. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Granfondo La Nucia’s 82 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Granfondo La Nucia. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Granfondo La Nucia rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, VO2max, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 82 miles of mixed terrain in La Nucia, Alicante, Spain.
